requirements.requirement: Configure the opsadmin account on node1 with the supplied SSH public key.
requirements.summary: The account exists with the expected home and shell, its password is locked, and authorized_keys contains exactly one line matching the supplied Ed25519 key. Ownership and permissions are appropriate, and the state persisted after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication for opsadmin.
requirements.summary: The effective live and post-reboot SSH policy enables public-key authentication, disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication, and sets AuthenticationMethods to publickey. SSH was listening and an authentication attempt without a key was rejected with only publickey offered.

overall_summary: Both public task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the SSH service, account, exact key, permissions, and policy recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No successful login using the corresponding private key was demonstrated; verification instead directly established the exact authorized key, effective key-only policy, live SSH endpoint, and rejection of keyless authentication.

operational_hygiene.summary: The account, key, SSH configuration, generated host keys, runtime directory, service activation, and reboot were causally connected to the task or mandatory restart verification. The failed initial activation partially applied necessary configuration and was corrected, so it is not an unnecessary mutation. One avoidable residue remained: cmd-b5db343e4e5647fd created /tmp/post-reboot-hostkeys for bounded verification but did not remove it; the after-executor snapshot confirms it remained. No failed services or package damage were observed.
